problems.title: The sum of both paths
problems.statement: An if/else has 10 instructions on the then path and 6 on the else path. Half the lanes of a warp take each side.

parts.prompt: Instructions the divergent warp issues for the if/else?
SIMD efficiency, in %?
Instructions a warp issues if all its lanes take the then path?

problems.solution: (a) $10 + 6 = 16$. (b) Useful: $16 \times 10 + 16 \times 6 = 256$; issued $16 \times 32 = 512$: 50%. (c) 10: uniform warps pay only for their own path.

problems.title: One slow lane, again
problems.statement: In a warp, 30 lanes run a loop 5 times and 2 lanes run it 50 times. The body is one instruction.

parts.prompt: Loop iterations the warp executes?
SIMD efficiency, in %?

problems.title: Which conditions diverge?

parts.prompt: Which conditions make at least one warp diverge?

problems.solution: Even/odd lanes split every warp. < 16 splits warp 0. (x/32)%2 and < 32 are constant within each warp. % 64 < 48 is true for 32–47 and false for 48–63: warp 1 splits.

problems.title: Nested divergence
problems.statement: In a full warp: if (lane < 16) { A; if (lane % 2) B; else C; } else { D; }. A, B, C and D cost 4, 3, 5 and 6 instructions.

parts.prompt: Instructions issued?
SIMD efficiency, in %?

hints: The then side runs A, B and C (B and C diverge too).
Useful: A on 16 lanes, B and C on 8 each, D on 16.
problems.solution: (a) $4 + 3 + 5 + 6 = 18$. (b) Useful $16\cdot4 + 8\cdot3 + 8\cdot5 + 16\cdot6 = 224$; issued $18 \times 32 = 576$: $38.9\%$. B and C run on a quarter of the warp each.

problems.title: The guard
problems.statement: A 1-D launch with 256-thread blocks and the guard if (i < n).

parts.prompt: For n = 1000: how many warps diverge at the guard?
For n = 1024?
For n = 1000: global index of the warp that diverges?

hints: Only a warp containing both i < n and i ≥ n diverges.
problems.solution: (a) $1000/32 = 31.25$: warp 31 holds 992–1023, split at 1000. Warps 0–30 are all true; warp 31 is the only one that straddles n. (b) None: 1024 is a multiple of 32, so every warp is uniform. (c) 31.

problems.title: Data decides
problems.statement: Each lane independently takes the then path (20 instructions) with probability 0.1, else the else path (4 instructions).

parts.prompt: Probability a warp is uniform, in %?
Expected instructions issued per warp?
If the data were sorted so every warp is uniform, expected instructions per warp?
Speedup from sorting (ignoring its cost)?

hints: Uniform: all false or all true.
problems.solution: (a) $0.9^{32} + 0.1^{32} = 3.43\%$. (b) $0.0343 \times 4 + 0.9657 \times 24 = 23.31$. (c) A tenth of warps pay 20 and the rest 4: 5.6. (d) 4.16×. A 10% branch makes almost every warp diverge; sorting turns that back into the work actually needed.

problems.title: Reconvergence points

parts.prompt: For if (c) { X; } else { Y; } Z;, the immediate post-dominator of the branch is…
For for (k = 0; k < m[i]; k++) { X; } Y; with m[i] varying per lane, lanes rejoin…
options: at Y, after the warp's longest-running lane finishes

hints: The first instruction every path must pass through.
problems.solution: (a) Z: both paths flow into it. (b) Y: lanes that finish early are masked until the last lane leaves the loop.

problems.title: Escape-time fractals
problems.statement: A Mandelbrot-style kernel: each lane iterates until its point escapes. Suppose iteration counts are independent and uniform on 1, …, 100.

parts.prompt: Expected iterations per lane?
Expected iterations a warp executes (the maximum of 32 lanes)?
Expected SIMD efficiency, in %?

problems.solution: (a) 50.5. (b) $\sum_{k=1}^{100} \big(1 - ((k-1)/100)^{32}\big) = 97.44$. (c) $51.8\%$. In real images neighbouring points have similar counts, so 2-D blocks that keep a warp's pixels close together do much better than this random model: spatial coherence is a divergence optimisation.

problems.title: Sort the rays?
problems.statement: A ray tracer shades 1M rays. Half hit material A (200 cycles of shading), half hit B (50 cycles), randomly mixed. Sorting rays by material costs the equivalent of 20 cycles per warp.

parts.prompt: Cycles per warp unsorted (assume every warp has both materials)?
Average cycles per warp after sorting, including the sort?
Speedup?

hints: Sorted warps are uniform: half pay 200, half 50.
problems.solution: (a) $200 + 50 = 250$. (b) $(200 + 50)/2 + 20 = 145$. (c) 1.72×. This is the trade-off behind Shader Execution Reordering: spend a little on data movement to buy back lanes.

problems.title: Independent thread scheduling
problems.statement: Volta and later give every thread its own program counter.

parts.prompt: Which statements are true?
options: Divergent paths still cost the sum of both paths
The two paths of a divergent branch may now interleave
Reconvergence is guaranteed at the immediate post-dominator
A spin-lock taken by one lane of a warp no longer has to deadlock

problems.solution: The issue hardware is unchanged, so divergence still serialises. Paths may interleave, reconvergence isn't guaranteed where the old stack would put it, and starvation-free lock algorithms become possible. Implicit-lockstep code is exactly what became unsafe.
